name: Saint Cajetan
history: A nobleman of Vicenza and a lawyer in the papal court, Cajetan became a priest and gave his life to reforming the clergy from within. In 1524 he founded the Theatines, priests who lived in poverty and trusted in Providence alone, refusing even to beg. He served the sick and the poor, and is the patron of those seeking work.
life: Gaetano dei Conti di Thiene took his doctorate in law at Padua and went to Rome to serve Pope Julius II. There he joined the Oratory of Divine Love, a confraternity of priests and laymen devoted to prayer and to care for the incurable sick, and was ordained in 1516. Grieved by the worldliness of many clergy, in 1524 he founded with Gian Pietro Carafa, the future Pope Paul IV, the Clerks Regular, called Theatines. They lived in strict poverty, owned nothing, did not beg, and relied on what Providence sent, while preaching, celebrating the liturgy well and caring for the sick. During the Sack of Rome in 1527 Cajetan was beaten by soldiers who wanted money he did not have. In Naples he worked among the poor and helped found a lending house to rescue them from usurers. He died there in 1547 and was canonised in 1671.
prayerTo: Saint Cajetan, you trusted the Father to feed His children and gave your life to the poor and the sick. Pray for all who are out of work or anxious about money, that they may find honest work and daily bread. Free me from worry, and teach me to seek first the Kingdom of God. Amen.
penance: Give something today to a food bank or a charity that helps people into work, and pray for someone you know who is looking for a job.
meditation: Cajetan would not let his priests beg, because he believed God already knew what they needed. What would change if you truly believed your Father knows what you need before you ask?
prayer: O God, Who bestowed upon St. Cajetan, Your Confessor, the grace to follow the apostolic way of life; grant us by his intercession and example ever to trust in You and to long only for the things of heaven. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
